selection: Panels a-d use three fixed NTT arithmetic primitives and two stage organizations; panels e-f use fixed NTT radix2-shoup shared-iterative local-layout controls at two batch sizes.
scope: A100; NTT word64 q576460756061519873, natural cyclic forward. Panels a-d use N=2^16,B=16 and fixed prefixes 256/1024; panels e-f use N=2^20, B=4/16, partition 10+10, and 256 threads. Only dataflow_layout changes in e-f; global I/O, stage partition, threads, arithmetic, and storage allocation remain fixed.
estimators: a ratio of three process medians; c same-provider resident median normalized to resident256 median; overlaid points/minmax use corresponding process pairs, not confidence intervals. e ratio of layout process medians; each layout point is its ordinary device latency divided by that batch linear median, with median and min/max; processes are independent, not recorded pairs. b complete-call DRAM byte reduction; d prefix node0 only; f sum of final two stage-kernel conflict counters from separate complete-NTT NCU captures, positive for reduction and negative for increase.
uncertainty: e three independent timing processes per layout and batch (12 total); ranges show observed process spread, not confidence intervals. NCU sums two final stage kernels per configuration in separate captures; clocks/cache uncontrolled. No profiler time enters performance.
alt_text: Six compact panels show NTT organization gains and resource costs. The lower controls compare linear and XOR shared layouts within one fixed NTT core at N=2^20 and B=4/16: XOR increases complete-call latency by about 4.7–7.4 percent, reduces shared-load conflicts by about 87 percent, and increases shared-store conflicts by about 13–14 percent.
